title: StrokeTutor Curriculum Catalog
description: Where each lesson lives in the curriculum. Kept beside the tutorials, never inside them: tutorial.schema.json says how a drawing plays, this says which path it belongs to, in what order, and how far through authoring it is. Catalog/paths.json is validated against definitions/pathsFile and Catalog/lessons.json against definitions/lessonsFile.

id.description: Lowercase slug. A lesson id is also the file name of its tutorial: Tutorials/<id>.json.

levels.description: Levels that group the paths, easiest first. Optional: a curriculum without levels is one flat list of paths. A level only groups and recommends; it never locks a path.

paths.description: Subject paths, in the order the learner sees them.

title.description: A name, not a number: "Starter", not "Level 1".

description.description: One line on what the paths of this level teach.

level.description: The id of the level this path belongs to. Must exist in levels. A path without one is listed after the levels.

lessonIds.description: Lessons in unlock order. Each must exist in lessons.json and belong to no other path.

status.description: Authoring state. Only approved lessons are meant to reach learners. A planned lesson holds a place in the curriculum before its tutorial exists; it is never published.

title.description: The lesson's name while it is planned. Required then. Once a tutorial exists, the tutorial's title is the lesson's name and this is dropped.

objective.description: One line: the single new idea this lesson teaches.

complexity.description: Relative difficulty inside the path, 1 (first lesson) to 5.

notes.description: Authoring notes for the creator. Never shown to learners.

generation.description: How the lesson was first generated, kept so prompts and models can be compared later. Never shown to learners.

reference.description: The real-world photo the lesson simplifies, with where it came from and the terms it may be used under.

file.description: File name inside Assets/References/. A bare name, so it can never point outside that folder.
